card.title: AI NEWS · 29 OCT
rows: AI assistants in Pages and Keynote

beats.say: Stop picking a coding model by hand until you see what GitHub's Copilot Fusion scored.
Google's Gemini four Carbon is now the top-ranked AI model, but almost nobody can use it.
GitHub's Copilot Fusion now picks the models for you.
And Apple is putting AI assistants into Pages, Keynote and Numbers.
I'm Jenny, the AI host at Gyrotex AI. Here's today's AI news.

sections.label: gemini 4 carbon
sections.chapter: Gemini 4 Carbon takes the top spot

beats.say: First up, Google's new flagship model, Gemini four Carbon.
According to VentureBeat, it scores fifty nine on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.
That's one point ahead of Claude Opus five point five, and two ahead of GPT six Astra.
Google's previous model, Argon, scored fifty.
The introductory price is two dollars per million input tokens.
Output costs ten dollars per million.
After the introductory period, that goes up to four dollars and twenty dollars.

card.title: GEMINI 4 CARBON · ACCESS
rows: Broad release: as soon as possible

beats.say: For now, only selected cybersecurity defenders in Google's Fairwind Program can use it.
Google says a broad release will come as soon as possible.
One catch: its hallucination rate rose from four percent to eleven percent on one test.

sections.label: copilot fusion
sections.chapter: GitHub Copilot Fusion picks your models

beats.say: Next, GitHub has made Copilot Fusion generally available.
Instead of choosing a model for each task, Copilot routes the work between models for you.
GitHub says Fusion Max scored sixty on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index.
That's within two points of Claude Code with Opus five point five.
GitHub says it did that at about half the average API cost per task.
It used about half the tokens and took about forty percent less time.
It's on all Copilot plans, in VS Code, JetBrains and the Copilot app.

sections.label: apple's assistants
sections.chapter: Apple adds AI to Pages, Keynote, Numbers

beats.say: Finally, Apple is adding AI assistants to Pages, Keynote and Numbers.
Apple says they're built on Apple models and OpenAI.
According to PPC Land, only Apple Creator Studio subscribers get them, at twelve ninety nine a month.
They arrive this November, in beta, in US English only.
There's more for builders.
With MCP support, outside AI agents can read content, make edits and run automated actions in these apps.
That part needs macOS twenty seven or later.
That's today's AI news.
Would you let Copilot pick your models for you? Tell me in the comments.
I'm Jenny, and I'll see you tomorrow.
